text:
incident-bot: PAGE: hf-artifact-fetch 5xx/429s detected for model fetches in us-west-2 — impact: cold-start failures and increased request latency. Pager duty: oncall-maya. https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/5543 :rotating_light:

sre-lee: seeing a spike of `model_fetch` errors on runtime nodes, lots of 429 returned from huggingface.co artifact CDN. Errors started ~1934567800 UTC, ramped up over last 2m. 

oncall-maya: acked. jumping in. first quick checks: are we hitting our own rate limits or HF?

ops-jen: grafana: `hhf.artifact.fetch.errors` jumped from ~0.1% to 12% across serving fleet, p95 cold-start latency 3.2s -> 12s. link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/xyz/model-fetch

infra-jay: curl against HF registry shows `HTTP/2 429` with body `You have exceeded the request quota` for bulk artifact endpoints. example: 
```
$ curl -i -H "User-Agent: redwood-inference/1.0" https://huggingface.co/api/models/rdw/llama-13b/artifacts
HTTP/2 429
content-type: application/json
{ "error": "rate limit exceeded" }
```

eng-anna: we have prefetch set to aggressive (concurrency 40) on new nodes; prefetch tasks could be spiking HF. disabling prefetch is quick mitigation.

sre-lee: good call. reducing prefetch concurrency to 4 for all new nodes now via runtime config: `prefetch.concurrency=4`. rolling out to 100% for new pool.

ops-jen: deployed config change, watching.

cs-tom: any customer-facing impact? I’ve got a thread from a small enterprise customer reporting elevated 5xxs on webhooks. We should draft an initial customer impact note.

oncall-maya: impact assessment: 429 from HF causes artifact fetch to fail on cold-start; warm cached instances unaffected. Customers with burst traffic or recent scale-ups see failed requests and timeouts. estimate: ~7% of production requests for last 5m affected. TTL: unknown until HF response.

incident-bot: updated incident state -> INVESTIGATING (severity: elevated). Pager: escalate if not resolved in 15m.

infra-jay: enabling fallback to internal artifact mirror (s3://rdw-model-cache) for any model with a cached copy. executing playbook step: `runtime.fallback.artifact_source = s3`

eng-anna: note: some models not cached yet (recently onboarded). for those, fallback to smaller quantized variant `llama-13b-q4_0` if available. pushing policy change now.

ops-jen: applied s3 fallback to 75% of requests; error rate dropped from 12% -> 3.6% in 90s. latency p95 improving.

sre-lee: opened HF support ticket via enterprise channel: ref 97531. included request ids, example 429 bodies, and our rate patterns. asked for temporary quota bump or explanation of sudden throttling.

eng-anna: running quick diff on recent deploys — we rolled a prefetch change last night to increase concurrency and also enabled a telemetry job that refreshes manifests every 20s. that combo could produce an amplified fetch load. rolling back telemetry refresh to 60s.

oncall-maya: performing handoff note for next on-call in 20m: current mitigations: reduced prefetch concurrency, s3 fallback enabled, fallback to q4 variant enabled, telemetry refresh throttled. HF ticket open (97531). KPI: target error rate <1% and p95 <5s.

vp-ops: any chance this is an auth provider issue? token refresh errors could also hit HF with unauthenticated calls.

infra-jay: checked auth logs — token refresh success rate stable. HF returns 429, not 401/403, so looks like quota throttle. Also saw delayed tracing to sentry: traces from the first 3m were delayed by ~40s due to observability vendor backlog, which slowed detection and correlation. filed ticket with vendor.

sre-lee: quick mitigation checklist added to thread: 
- disable aggressive prefetch (done)
- enable s3 fallback (done)
- promote cached model variants (done)
- increase runtime backoff on artifact GETs: `backoff.max_retries=6 backoff.jitter=true` (deploying)
- post incident: add soft rate limiter per-worker to avoid sudden fan-out

eng-anna: pushing runtime change: exponential backoff + jitter now in prod (rolling 30s). also added header `X-RDW-Artifact-Request: 1` to help HF correlate.

ops-jen: HF support replied: "we're investigating an internal edge-side rate limiter triggered by a recent HF infra deploy; we've temporarily increased quota for your org and will follow up with root cause in 4-6h."

cs-tom: drafting customer communication: short note acknowledging partial errors for cold starts between 1934567800-1934568040 UTC, mitigation in place (fallbacks), ask affected customers to contact support if they see persistent errors. will circulate.

oncall-maya: handing off to oncall-next (sre-lee) at 1934568010. leaving a short summary and action items in #oncall-handoff.

incident-bot: user sre-lee assigned as incident owner. escalation timer set 15m.

sre-lee: taking over. monitoring HF ticket and our error rate. plan: keep s3 fallback + prefetch limits for 2 hours, then slowly ramp up prefetch while monitoring HF feedback. prepare postmortem with timeline and quant metrics.

eng-anna: added a temporary dashboard panel for `artifact.fetch.429` by region + model to help root-cause model-specific hot-spots.

ops-jen: by 1934568040 UTC error rate down to 0.9%, p95 latency 3.6s. mitigation effective.

vp-ops: good containment. next: postmortem owners? suggest eng-anna (root cause), infra-jay (runbook gaps), cs-tom (customer comms).

sre-lee: agreed. tagging action items: 
1) postmortem + timeline (eng-anna).
2) implement per-worker soft rate limiter + backpressure (eng-runtime).
3) ensure prefetch default conservatism and add safety circuit (infra).
4) mirror-population audit: ensure all production models have an s3 cache copy (sre).
5) observability vendor SLA/backup for trace delays (ops).

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> partial remediation achieved. Incident remains open until HF follow-up.

cs-tom: sent customer note to impacted list; call scheduled with top-3 affected accounts at 1934568800 UTC.

eng-anna: quick note for the postmortem draft: HF edge limiter triggered by a recent HF deploy + our aggressive prefetch/manifest refresh produced request amplification. add timeline and numbers (total artifact requests vs baseline).

sre-lee: capturing logs and export of fetch request ids for HF. saving runbook gaps where the original detection alert threshold was too high.

oncall-maya: thanks team — handing off full context. leave any follow-ups in this thread.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: HF confirmed quota bump and a fix deployed on their side at 1934568095 UTC. Recommended follow-ups: postmortem, default prefetch tuning, soft rate limiter, ensure s3 mirror coverage.

vp-ops: closing note: good response and fast mitigations. let's make the postmortem clear on ownership and actionable deadlines.

sre-lee: creating postmortem doc and will link here when ready.
